primary_sources.title: Course in General Linguistics
primary_sources.why_relevant: This is the most cited and discussed work of Saussure, compiled from his students' lecture notes and published posthumously. It is considered the starting point of 20th-century structural linguistics and introduces key concepts like langue and parole, and the synchronic vs. diachronic approach to language study.

primary_sources.title: Mémoire sur le système primitif des voyelles dans les langues indo-européennes
primary_sources.why_relevant: This monograph, published during Saussure's lifetime, established his early reputation in comparative linguistics and focused on Indo-European languages.

primary_sources.title: Writings in General Linguistics
primary_sources.why_relevant: This volume contains some of Saussure's manuscripts, including an unfinished essay discovered in 1996, offering direct insight into his thought processes and ideas.

secondary_sources.title: Ferdinand de Saussure - Britannica
secondary_sources.why_relevant: This article provides a comprehensive overview of Saussure's life, his major contributions to linguistics and semiotics, and the foundational concepts of his theories, such as structuralism, langue/parole, and the arbitrary nature of the linguistic sign.

secondary_sources.title: Ferdinand de Saussure - StudySmarter
secondary_sources.why_relevant: This resource offers a biography of Saussure, explains his key theories, and discusses his most important works, including the challenges in translating his concepts.

secondary_sources.title: Ferdinand de Saussure - Wikipedia
secondary_sources.why_relevant: Wikipedia provides a detailed biographical account of Saussure, outlining his education, career, and the development and impact of his key ideas, such as structural linguistics and semiotics.

parsed.notes: Ferdinand de Saussure (1857-1913) was a Swiss linguist whose work laid the foundation for modern linguistics and structuralism. His most influential work, 'Course in General Linguistics,' was published posthumously and introduced concepts such as the distinction between 'langue' (language system) and 'parole' (individual speech), and the idea that linguistic signs are arbitrary. His ideas have had a profound impact on linguistics, semiotics, anthropology, and literary criticism.
